report:
I've taken c53's fed vortices end to end: the world now loads in the PhySim task as a lab bundle, with a frozen 15-program suite and 2 truths per case. A 64-member native reference earns reward **0.726** at K=2, and every validation step passed without credits. All mechanism controls fail on their targeted programs, but I could not build a clean division-specific control. Code is committed on `feat/labkit-worlds` (0e8c3dc, cea06cc), not pushed; total CPU was about 3.55 h and nothing touched Prime.

## 1. Behaviour under the chosen noise
Two fresh seeds ran to t=3000 at intensity 0.003, ell 2 (vorticity additive, fuel proportional), analysed with the curation `analyze.py`. Splitting does not stop, so I did not need the 0.001 fallback.

| seed | persistent splits | max generation | same-sign daughters | after t=1000 / 2000 | last split |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | 49 | 10 | 49/49 | 33 / 20 | 2916 |
| 22 | 36 | 12 | 36/36 | 27 / 16 | 2922 |

The noise-free claim was 34–42 splits at generation 9–10. Merge/split stays near 1 and 25–30 bodies remain at t=3000. I looked at `behav/behav_noise.png`: discrete vortices of both signs, with rods pinching late in the run.

## 2. Ports and envelope
- **Inject ports** (public order): (om,−), (Y,+), (om,+), (Y,−). Gains are 0.01 for vorticity and 0.1 for fuel, with fuel clipped at 0.
- **Envelope** (amp 3 for 50 tu at the worst site): everything stays finite. Vorticity stays in [−0.33, 0.40] (natural body peaks are about 0.22). Fuel stays in [0, 2.4], i.e. above its natural level of about 1 only where fuel is fed.
  - (Y,−) on a vortex starves it to zero within the window.
  - A fuel gain of 0.03 barely changes anything in 50 tu.
- **Observed ports:** vorticity, fuel, plus eating rate and flow speed as observe-only channels. The extra two are needed because PhySim's scorer has a single port count for both inject ports and observed channels, so the two must be equal (4).

## 3. Mechanism-targeted programs
- **Feeding alone does not cause division within 50 tu.** I tried six isolated vortices with centre, both-ends and neck-starvation programs. Fed vortices double their circulation, spin up and round off instead of dividing.
- **So the division programs act on a rod that is already pinching.** I prepared the state from init(31) to t=580 under the declared noise, with device 0 on the rod's neck. Device 1 sits on a vortex that drifts about 12 units in 50 tu, and moves are scaled to 3 world units per unit of `u`. Behaviour on the rod is the same in two noise members:
  - left alone it pinches into two same-sign daughters at about 23 tu;
  - feeding the neck suppresses the pinch;
  - starving the neck pinches it at about 8 tu;
  - feeding from t=10 delays it to 32–35 tu.
- **Device-1 programs** (`mech/targeted_strips.png`, which I looked at):
  - feeding: circulation roughly doubles (9.3 → 21.7 at 25 tu);
  - starving: the vortex is gone by about 25 tu;
  - om− cut: a remnant survives and regrows by eating;
  - follow: the centre node holds 0.18 for 50 tu, against 0.003 without following.
- **No clean division-specific control.**
  - A body-uniform gain (each body's growth replaced by its circulation-weighted mean) still pinches at 25–26 tu instead of 23–24. That means the pinch is strain thinning plus decay below the body threshold, not uneven feeding along the rod.
  - Smoothing the gain's saturation (σ 2–3) kills every body within 50 tu.
  - Smoothing the fuel in the growth term (σ 6) runs away to non-finite values.
  - Lowering the body threshold makes bodies decay.
  - The same sub-threshold decay shapes every body's edge and kills starved bodies, so I found no local change that removes pinching while keeping growth and motion. I kept the body-uniform gain as a control anyway.

## 4. Frozen suite
The suite has 8 generic PhySim-style programs and 7 targeted ones. Score groups are one per sensor and observed port (12 in total), with scales frozen from 12 calibration members before any truth. Controls use 4 members. Ratios are against the mean of 16 independent 4-member slices of the 64-member reference; the native band for the aggregate is 0.94–1.05.

| control | cases | ratio | 90% CI | cases beyond band |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ignore actions | 15 | 11.75 | 8.7–14.9 | 14 (sham ≈ 1.03) |
| wrong probe geometry | 15 | 13.5 | 12.6–14.5 | 15 |
| initial persistence | 15 | 23.6 | 21.5–25.9 | 15 |
| flow off (adv 0) | 15 | 116 | 109–123 | 15 |
| fuel regrowth off (kF 0) | 15 | 154 | 146–163 | 15 |
| body-uniform gain | 15 | 12.2 | 11.0–13.6 | 15 |
| dt-halved null | 15 | 1.02 | 0.98–1.06 | 1 (stir_cut 1.16 vs band max 1.15) |
| growth off (k 0) | 5 | 238 | 210–273 | 5 |
| decay off (mu 0) | 5 | 1989 | 1782–2173 | 5 |

Growth off and decay off ran only on their targeted programs and the sham, to save CPU.

Each control on its targeted program, against that case's band maximum (all fail):

| program | control: ratio |
|---|---|
| feed_neck | body gain 19.5, growth off 224 (band max 1.31) |
| starve_neck | body gain 12.8, decay off 2180 (1.26) |
| feed_vortex | growth off 272 (1.27) |
| starve_vortex | decay off 2137 (1.26) |
| stir_cut | growth off 185, decay off 1578 (1.15) |
| follow_vortex | flow off 122 (1.11) |
| feed_and_follow | flow off 143, growth off 308 (1.35) |

These ablations change the whole box, so they fail everywhere, sham included. The targeted programs raise the ratio by at most about 2× over the sham (body gain 19.5 on feed_neck against 10.2 on the sham).

**Groups the evaluation should not rely on:**
- **Device-0 groups for numerics:** the dt-halved null leaves their band on 2–5 cases; device0/eat is 1.11 against a band of 0.90–1.10. The pinch timing carries the time-step error.
- **Global groups for wrong probe geometry:** they cannot see probe positions, so they stay inside the band on up to 12 programs.
- **Each device's groups for ignore-actions** on programs that act only at the other device. Exception: the neck-feeding programs do reach device 1.

**Reward** (`rewards.py`, K=2 from `reward-calibration.json`): the 64-member reference scores 0.0353 through the evaluation path, giving reward 0.726. Initial persistence scores 1.026, giving 0. PhySim's calibration rule would give K=1 for this suite, under which the reference earns the full reward of 1; keeping K=2 would need scales about 10× the calibration standard deviations.

## 5. Lab bundle (`physim/labbundle.py`)
- **What it holds:** the world file verbatim, the labkit modules it imports, an observables module, the declaration, the apparatus, the prepared fields plus `t` (no pickle), the suite, truths and a checks file. All files and the implementation (runner, adapter, devices, scorer and bundle sources; numpy/scipy versions) are hashed into the bundle identity.
- **How it plugs in:** `LabBundle` subclasses `Bundle`, and `open_bundle` picks it when the manifest declares a lab world. `taskset.required_bundle` now goes through `open_bundle`.
- **Bundle:** `bundle:sha256:d5698a58…`. The suite file is 1.49 MB against the 2 MB JSON cap.

Validation without credits:
- `required_bundle` opens it as a `LabBundle` in both profiles.
- `public_prompt` renders ports 0–3, 4 channels and shape `(n, t, 4, slots)`. The spec never claims inject port p drives channel p, which is correct here.
- `LaboratoryTools.experiment` and `usage` were called directly (only the copy into the agent's container was skipped). A valid request is admitted and charged 20 tu; port 4 is rejected without charge.
- Two truths re-simulate bit for bit.
- Initial persistence reproduces the checks file through `reference_demo`, and the native reference is graded via `_forecast_suite`.
- Tampering is caught: an edited world file and a mismatched port roster are both refused.

## What is not established
- **One prepared state and apparatus.** The division programs depend on that particular rod, and the follow path was fitted to the native sham.
- **No fed-vortex control is specific to one mechanism**; all of them separate on every program.
- **Small samples:** controls use 4 members (bands from slices), and growth off / decay off ran on 5 cases each.
- **The device-0 null margin is thin**, and I did not re-test refinement at this preparation.
- **Not yet wired for lab bundles:** `hub.fetch_bundle` and `cli.py` still build Blobkit bundles directly.
- **Trust and fragility:** a lab bundle runs its world file in the grader's process, and any edit to `labworld.py` or `labbundle.py` (including by the other agent) invalidates the bundle until its manifest is rewritten.
- **No real agent rollout** has been run against it.

Everything is in /home/user/evalwork/vortex_eval; the bundle, `work/report.md` and `validate/validation.json` are under `suite/`. Code:
- /home/user/swpo/residency-environments/environments/physim/physim/labbundle.py
- /home/user/swpo/residency-environments/environments/physim/physim/taskset.py (the hook)
- /home/user/swpo/residency-environments/scripts/physim/labworlds/fedvortex_bundle.py
- /home/user/swpo/residency-environments/scripts/physim/labworlds/fedvortex_report.py
- /home/user/swpo/residency-environments/scripts/physim/labworlds/fedvortex_validate.py
- /home/user/swpo/residency-environments/scripts/physim/labworlds/fedvortex/ (observables and ablations)
- /home/user/swpo/residency-environments/environments/physim/LABWORLDS.md (new section)
check:
**Review of vortex_eval (c53 fed vortices): mostly confirmed, but I found one bug that must be fixed before any rollout uses this bundle.**

The reported numbers match the files. One truth re-simulates bit for bit, and the default Blobkit bundle path is unchanged. The bug is that the bundle breaks after it is copied. Also, the mechanism-targeting claim is weaker than the headline says, and one "independent" control is not independent.

**What I ran** (about 3 CPU-minutes, no credits)
- **Repo tests:** `uv run --quiet pytest tests -q` gives 7 passed. These tests only build packages; nothing in them exercises physim.
- **Blobkit path by hand:**
  - The only change to `taskset.py` is `Bundle(...)` → `open_bundle(...)`, and `bundles.py` is untouched.
  - For a Blobkit-schema manifest and for a missing manifest, `open_bundle` raises the same errors as `Bundle`.
  - `physim.taskset` imports.
- **Truth re-simulation:** opened the bundle, called `make_oracle`, and re-simulated truth c014 (follow_vortex, 2 members, 14 CPU-s). All three query arrays match the stored truth exactly.
- **Re-scoring:** with my own script calling `score_case`, I re-scored the reference, the 16 slices, the body-gain, dt-halved and wrong-geometry controls on sham, feed_neck and stir_cut. The 64-member reference energy, the bands and the ratios all match `report.json` exactly (for example body gain 19.47 on feed_neck and 10.15 on sham; null 1.161 against band maximum 1.151 on stir_cut).
- **Behaviour runs:** the JSON files confirm the table. Seed 21: 49 persistent splits, generation 10, 49/49 same-sign, last split at 2916. Seed 22: 36 splits, generation 12, 36/36, last at 2922.
- **World files:** `world.py` and `labkit/ops.py` in the bundle are byte-identical to c53's file and to labkit.
- **Reward:** confirmed. −log10(0.03532)/2 = 0.726. The calibration rule gives K=1 because the worst native case is 0.048.
- **Freeze order:** calibration (04:13:10 to 04:14:09), then `suite.json` (04:14:10), then truths (04:14:24 to 04:17:47), then controls (from 04:18). Seeds are separated through the sha256 member-seed mapping.
- **Same prepared state:** all controls are built with `bundle.make_oracle(world=..., devices=...)`, so they start from the same prepared state.
- **Image:** I looked at `mech/targeted_strips.png`. The rod pinches around 20–25 tu in the sham, feeding the neck suppresses the pinch, starving the neck pinches it early, and the starved vortex is gone by about 25 tu.

**Findings**

1. **The bundle breaks after a plain copy (must fix).**
   - **Cause:** `write_manifest` hashes everything under `world/` (`rglob("*")`). That included `world/__pycache__/world.cpython-312.pyc` and `observables.cpython-312.pyc`, which Python wrote when the build loaded the world.
   - **Reproduced:** after `cp -r bundle /tmp/fvcopy`, which gives the files new modification times, the first open works. `make_oracle` then rewrites the stale .pyc files: the world.pyc hash goes from b96374… to 9e2a1a…. The next `open_bundle` fails with `BundleError: ... world/__pycache__/observables.cpython-312.pyc`.
   - **Effect:** any fetch, git checkout or upload of the bundle will fail on its second `required_bundle` call. Grading after the tools have run would be one such call. Validation only passed because it ran in place.
   - **Fix:**
     - Skip `__pycache__` in `write_manifest`.
     - Refuse `__pycache__` paths in `validate_lab_manifest`.
     - Set `sys.dont_write_bytecode` while `LabBundle` loads world files.
     - Then rewrite the manifest. This changes `bundle_id`; the truths stay the same.

2. **The targeted programs do not single out their mechanisms.** Every ablation is at least 10× native on every case, so the "fails on its targeted program against the band" test is passed trivially. Dividing each ablation's ratio by its own sham ratio shows how little targeting there is:

   | ablation | targeted program: ratio ÷ sham ratio |
   |---|---|
   | growth off (k 0) | feed_vortex 1.17, feed_neck 0.96, stir_cut 0.79 |
   | decay off (mu 0) | starve_vortex 1.08, starve_neck 1.10, stir_cut 0.80 |
   | flow off (adv 0) | follow_vortex 1.12; the generic two_sources is higher at 1.39 |
   | body-uniform gain | feed_neck 1.92 (largest of all cases), feed_vortex 1.64 |

   - Only the body-gain control on feed_neck shows any targeting.
   - Most of the size of these ratios comes from the global groups, whose scales are tiny (global mean scales 3.8e-4 to 3.7e-3). For example, regrowth off gives about 150–360 on global groups but 11–74 on device groups. Decay off reaches 5221 on global/om.
   - These ablations behave more like different worlds than mechanism probes. The report half-says this ("at most about 2× over the sham"), but its opening claim that all mechanism controls fail on their targeted programs overstates it.

3. **The "independent native" control is not independent.** `fedvortex_report.py` sets `controls["independent_native"] = slices[0]`, which is one of the 16 slices that define the band and the denominator. Its "0 beyond band" result therefore cannot fail. The real independent null is the dt-halved run (seeds 82000+i). It leaves the band on 1 of 15 cases, close to the about 0.9 expected by chance, since each case's band is the extremes of 16 slices.

4. **Minor points.**
   - The 4-member controls reuse the reference seeds (81000+i), so they share noise with slice 0. This does not bias the scores.
   - `LabWorld.load` leaves `bundle/world` at `sys.path[0]` in the grader process for the rest of the run, where its `world`, `observables` and `labkit` can shadow other modules.
   - The native reference is about 27× less sharp than PhySim's (worst case 0.048 against 0.0018). Under the calibrated rule (K=1) the native reward saturates at 1; K=2 needs scales about 9.6× larger, as the report says.

**What is not established by this review:** I did not re-run any control ensembles, the envelope tests, the division-specific control attempts, or the long behaviour simulations.

**Verdict:** the evaluation path, freeze order, seed independence, truth reproducibility and the Blobkit default all check out. Fix item 1 before the bundle leaves this directory. Present the controls as world-level separations, not as tests of individual mechanisms. Drop "independent native" or replace it with a fresh native ensemble.

Files are in /home/user/evalwork/vortex_review:
- recheck.py
- truthcmp.py
- pyc.py
- which.py

report:
I've finished all four items. Both suites are frozen, with truths and controls, but every control ensemble has only 4 members, so read single-case ratios with care. The PM noise question has an answer: intensity 0.01 at dt 0.5 is admissible for the suite's 2–50 tu groups but not for short-lead scoring at the pulse site. CIPS-iso passes parity and envelope; its dt null is borderline at 1.12, just above the native-vs-native band. CPU used is about 3.5 h of the 4 h budget. No Prime or model calls were made, and labworld.py and labeval.py are unedited.

## 1. phase_membrane noise
The test used the K pulse at device0 from the earlier prepared state (`prep_s0`). Settings: intensity 0.01, ell 2, dt 0.5 (2 steps per tick), with a dt/4 null (dt 0.25). I ran three native ensembles of 8, two independent null ensembles of 8 and an ignore-actions ensemble of 8, then compared them over 2000 random partitions of the natives.

| window / group | native band 5–95% | null N1 | null N2 | 16-member null vs 16 natives | ignore-actions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 tu, all groups | 0.91–1.10 | 1.08 (36% above band) | 0.99 (1%) | **1.03 (1.4%)** | 3.2 |
| 50 tu, device1 | 0.87–1.15 | 1.18 (55%) | 0.97 | 1.08 (18%) | 0.95 |
| ≤10 tu, device0 (pulse site) | 0.92–1.10 | 1.11 | 1.11 | **1.10 (51%)** | 106 |

- **What remains is first-order error in the K-pulse response.** At zero noise the dt error at device0/K is 0.84 member sd in the first 10 tu and 0.22 over 50 tu; everything else is ≤ 0.17.
- **Comparison with earlier settings:** at dt 1 the pulse-site figure was 1.34; at intensity 0.03 the null was 1.04–1.08.
- **Cost:** 16.8 s per 50-tu member (2× native dt 1); the null costs 32.4 s per member.
- **Verdict:** admissible for 2–50 tu groups; do not score device0 at ≤10 tu on K-pulse programs.
- **Not settled — global groups.** The suite's own null shows global 1.02–1.38, and 1.4–2.0 on the sham case alone, against a band of 0.94–1.08. A zero-noise sham check finds a small but real dt bias in the box statistics (global L variance 0.70 member sd, K variance 0.37).
- **Not rerun:** the nucleation count at dt 0.5. The dt-1 runs at 0.01 had none.

## 2. CIPS-iso
- **World variant:** `worlds/cips_iso.py` is c40 with only the enzyme drift replaced by the isotropic stencil.
  - After 300 steps its e, p and F are bit-identical to the earlier `world_iso.py`. The amphiphile is one-way coupled, so the chance-level division axes found there carry over.
  - The amphiphile drift keeps its original axis-only scheme, as you specified. Its isotropy was not checked.
- **Prepared state:** seed 5 at t = 3100, zero noise, 5 bodies. Device0 and device1 sit on the necks of two dumbbells that pinch about 20 and 34 tu into the window.
- **Parity:** the runner matches the native module exactly (max difference 0.0 on fields and readouts over 50 tu), and members are identical at zero noise.
- **Envelope:** amp 3 for 50 tu at each device, with gains of 1 on p, F and s: everything stays finite and in range (e ≤ 1.0, p ≤ 0.87, F ≥ 0.058, s ≤ 83).
- **Noise level (ell 2, proportional on all four fields):**
  - 0.01 and 0.03 keep the two divisions (5 → 7 bodies) with e ≤ 0.988.
  - 0.1 pushes e above 1 (1.015–1.025), so it is out.
  - **I chose 0.03.**
- **dt null:**
  - At gain 1, the injection is clipped every step (p at 1, F at 0). The pulse-site error is then 9–35 member sd; for example, F under the fuel cut reads 0.060 at dt 0.1 against 0.027 at dt 0.05.
  - At gain 0.3 it falls to 0.6–3.2 sd in the first 10 tu (feeding is worst) and 0.2–1.1 over 50 tu. The amphiphile at gain 1 stays ≤ 0.15.
  - **I chose gains p 0.3, F 0.3 (both signs), s 1.**
  - Suite null (3 cases): **1.12 [1.09–1.15]** against a band of 1.05 [0.97–1.11]. Even the sham case is 1.4 / 1.3 at the two devices, so CIPS at dt 0.1 is borderline. Halving dt would cost 2× (null 4×).
- **Cost:** 25 s per member, 50 s per null member.

## 3. Mechanisms, programs and their controls
Pilots ran at zero noise; I looked at the field images.

**phase_membrane**
- Links at the cell centre grow it and split it by 50 tu. With the tilt halved (`a2`) it only elongates; with adsorption off (`chi0`) no link ring forms and the cell shrinks.
- Feeding the starved big cell keeps it whole; in the sham it breaks up within 10 tu.
- Starving the small cell dissolves it by 10 tu; in the sham it dissolves by about 30 tu.

**CIPS**
- Product or fuel at a neck holds the neck: no division within 50 tu.
- A fuel cut at a neck makes it pinch within 5–10 tu.
- Amphiphile pulsed at the neck collects at the interface.

The table gives each control's score ratio on its own program (sham in brackets). The last column isolates the part of the failure caused by the program: how differently the control responds to the program than the native does, in native member sd. Other probes show ≤ 0.9 sd. Ratios are from the suite, at the chosen noise.

| claim | control | program | ratio (sham) | response difference at the program's probe (native response) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PM: links tilt phase, hold the wall | tilt halved (a2) | L_d0 / L_rim / L_d1 | 6.6 / 10.7 / 13.3 (10.2) | 3.5 / 4.0 / 8.2 (7.1 / 7.2 / 8.4) |
| PM: links adsorb at the wall | chi0 | L_d0 / L_rim | 6.9 / 11.8 (11.3) | 4.2 / 3.4 |
| PM: division by central starvation | substrate diffusion doubled (DS2) | Sp_d0 / Sm_d1 / Sp_d1 | 14.0 / 15.7 / 13.2 (11.7) | 4.1 / 4.9 / 5.4 |
| CIPS: enzyme condenses up its product | chi0 | p_d0 | 100 (88); device0 52 vs 21 | 19.9 (33.1) |
| CIPS: catalysis burns regrowing fuel | kF0 | Fp_d0 | 289 (264) | 15.7 (22.9) |
| CIPS: amphiphile layer | chis0 | s_d0 | 13.0 (10.6) | 3.2 at device0; 19.3 global |
| CIPS: division needs turnover | d0 | Fm_d0 | 22 (26); device0 5.7 vs 13.9 | 13.4 (17.2) |
| CIPS: starvation under a local fuel cut | fuel diffusion ×10 (DF10) | Fm_d0 | 77 (83); device0 29 vs 21 | 18.1 (17.2) |

- **Every matching control fails on its program, and the extra error sits at the probe the program acts on.** But all the full ablations already fail heavily on the sham, so a per-case ratio mostly reflects that, not the program.
- **Changes from the planned controls:**
  - A 10× substrate feed turned the whole box into inside phase, so I replaced it with doubled substrate diffusion.
  - No world parameter removes local fuel starvation alone, so fuel diffusion ×10 stands in for it.
- **Division is not seen cleanly in phase_membrane.** In this prepared state, starvation shows up as break-up and dissolution, not as clean binary division in the window.

## 4. Frozen suites
**Set-up**
- Programs: 14 for phase_membrane, 12 for CIPS.
- Score scales frozen from a calibration ensemble before any truth; 2 truths per case.
- 4-member controls; ablations ran on sham plus their matching programs only.
- Second native ensemble (the band) on 5 PM and 4 CIPS cases; null on 3 cases with its own seeds.
- `labeval.py` is used unchanged for scales, groups, caching and scoring. The suite file is labeval's format plus extra keys (`programs`, `case_controls`, `band_seeds`, `null_seeds`), schema `labeval-v1+pmcips1`; the calibration is sham ×2 plus each single-pulse program.

| control | PM ratio [90%] | CIPS ratio [90%] |
|---|---|---|
| band (native vs native) | 0.99 [0.81–1.23] | 1.05 [0.97–1.11] |
| ignore actions | 3.63 [2.93–4.43] | 4.73 [3.64–5.86] |
| wrong probe geometry | 2.42 [2.17–2.71] | 6.72 [6.19–7.34] |
| initial persistence | 9.96 [9.04–11.0] | 8.15 [6.96–9.48] |
| mechanism ablations | 9.5–13.5 | 11.8–276 |
| dt null | 0.99 [0.91–1.05] | 1.12 [1.09–1.15] |

**Groups not to rely on**
- Wrong probe geometry: all global groups, in both worlds (by construction).
- PM ignore-actions: global S, K and phi. Device1 also does not separate on device0-only programs.
- PM: the global groups also carry the dt penalty (section 1).
- CIPS `chis0`: every group except the amphiphile's (exactly 1.00, because the amphiphile does not act back on anything).
- Single programs that do not test actions: a 1-unit probe shift (ignore-actions 1.07 in PM, 1.46 in CIPS).
- Per-case ratios below about 1.5: the per-case band runs from 0.70 to 1.46.

**64-member reference:** not affordable. It would take about 4.2 CPU-h for PM (14 cases × 64 × 16.8 s) and about 5.3 CPU-h for CIPS.

## Not established
- Ablations were not run on every mechanism program, so there is no full control × program matrix.
- One prepared state per world; 4-member controls.
- CIPS-iso's refined-grid and rotation checks were not rerun under noise.

## Change needed in labworld.py
I did not make this change; this is a description. `LabStepper` adds each source as `+gain·amp·h·bump` once per native step, before the world's step, then clips. For ports that clip, or fields that diffuse fast (CIPS fuel spreads across the source width about 4.5 times per time unit), the response at the pulse site then depends on dt at first order. A fix would add:
- an opt-in mode that hands the source to the world, so it enters the world's implicit diffusion solve;
- a saturating sink for negative actuators on non-negative fields, instead of the clip.

Separately, the scoring roster ties the number of actuators to the number of observed ports. That forced CIPS down to four actuators (p+, F+, F−, s+), so the enzyme cannot be driven.

## Commits (branch `feat/labkit-worlds`, not pushed)
- `2fc1d4d`: `scripts/physim/labworlds/worlds/cips_iso.py` and `scripts/physim/labworlds/pmcips.py` (declarations, programs, suite freeze/run/report).
- `e2b1451`: `scripts/physim/labworlds/pmcips_runs/` (the run scripts).
- Runs used a pinned copy of the physim package at `e64fbf2`; labworld.py is unchanged since then.

## Files
Everything is in `/home/user/evalwork/pm_cips_eval`:
- `pm_noise/analysis.json`
- `cips_accept/` (parity, envelope, noise and dt-screen files)
- `suite_pm/report.md`, `suite_cips/report.md`
- `suite_*/specificity.json`
- `figs/pilot_*.png`
check:
**Review of pm_cips_eval (phase_membrane and CIPS-iso suites)**

**Verdict:** The report's numbers are accurate and I reproduced them. The suites are sound as curation evidence. Three things need settling before rollouts: the enzyme going above 1 under CIPS noise, the PM global groups, and the CIPS dt null. The claim that each control fails specifically on its own program is weaker than the report says. I used about 2 CPU-minutes.

**What I checked and confirmed**

**Problems**
1. **CIPS enzyme goes above 1 at the chosen noise (not in the report).** The CIPS envelope was run at zero noise only. At intensity 0.03, the product-pulse programs push e above 1 at the probes:
   - truth c004 (p_d0): 1.0028
   - independent_native: 1.0018
   - band: 1.0009
   - truth c005 (p_d1): 1.0011

   e is a volume fraction, the step does not clip it, and the e(1−e) mobility turns negative above 1. Intensity 0.1 was rejected for exactly this. Fix: a noise form bounded on e (for example scaled by e(1−e)), or accept it explicitly with a note.
2. **Mechanism specificity is not established.**
   - Ablations ran only on the sham and their own programs, so there is no evidence about how they fail on other programs.
   - In 4 of the 11 program pairs the control's ratio on its own program is lower than on the sham: PM a2/L_d0 6.6 vs 10.2; PM chi0/L_d0 6.9 vs 11.3; CIPS d0/Fm_d0 22 vs 26 (device0 5.7 vs 13.9); CIPS DF10/Fm_d0 77 vs 83.
   - kF0, chi0 and DF10 already fail 80–290× on the sham, so they behave as "a different world", not as tests of one mechanism.
   - Specificity rests only on the response-difference measure. "Other probes ≤ 0.9 sd" holds for the other device, roughly the noise level with 4-member ensembles. It does not hold for the global sensor: kF0 5.3, DF10 4.1, a2/L_d1 2.0, chi0/L_d0 1.2.
3. **Intervals rest on very few cases.** Each CIPS ablation interval comes from 2 cases, so [88–100] is just the two values. The band uses 5 cases (PM) and 4 (CIPS). Treat these as descriptive.
4. **PM noise verdict is lenient and incomplete.**
   - The "16-member null 1.03 (1.4%)" is compared with an 8-vs-8 band. That band is wider than a 16-member one would be, so the test is easy to pass.
   - The band comes from 2000 partitions of the same 24 natives, and the check used one program (the K pulse).
   - The suite's own null puts the global groups at 1.02–1.38 (sham 1.75) against a band of 0.94–1.08. Yet the global groups still carry equal weight in the frozen PM suite (4 of 12). Before rollouts, either exclude or flag the global groups for PM scoring, or halve dt again.
5. **CIPS dt null is above the band, and noise was partly chosen to hide it.**
   - `cips_gains.json` says 0.03 was preferred partly because it makes the dt error 3× smaller relative to the member spread.
   - Even so, the null is 1.12 [1.09–1.15] with 3 of 3 cases worse, against a band upper bound of 1.11; device0 on the sham is 1.38.
   - By the standard applied elsewhere this is not admissible. Halving dt costs 2× per member (4× for the null).
6. **PM prepared-state path is fragile.** `PM_PREP` defaults to a `/tmp` scratchpad path. The copy in `pm_prep/prep_s0.npz` has the same sha256 (`c463826b…`), which `suite.json` records. Change the default to the copy.
